overview: Each partition is an append-only segment log on a leader broker with followers; producers with acks=all wait for the ISR; a Raft-based controller assigns leaders; consumer groups commit offsets to an internal topic.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative ingest: 100K records/s at 1 KB each.
estimation.calculation: 100,000 × 1 KB ≈ 100 MB/s; at 10 MB/s per partition, ≥10 partitions before headroom.
estimation.result: Three replica copies imply roughly 300 MB/s of storage writes before overhead.
estimation.implication: Partition count must cover throughput and consumer parallelism; retention dominates disk sizing.

components.purpose: acks=all waits for the in-sync replicas
components.rationale: Use timeouts, authenticated requests and idempotency when supported; define ambiguous outcomes.

components.purpose: Partitions are append-only logs; leader + followers (ISR), min.insync.replicas=2, fsync batched; retention 7 days or compaction
components.rationale: Ordering is within a partition; checkpoint only after durable effects and dedup replays.
Use a quorum and fencing; possession of an expired lease must never authorize a stale writer.

components.purpose: Commit offsets to an internal topic; rebalancing on join/leave
components.rationale: Assume retries; identify work stably, fence obsolete attempts and commit results before acknowledgement.

accessPatterns: Append by partition; read sequentially from an offset.
constraints: Offsets order only one partition; dedup producer sequence after retries.

entityDetails.purpose: Consumer-group progress for replay and recovery.
accessPatterns: Commit progress after processing; resume after rebalance.
constraints: An ack before processing risks loss; processing before ack implies duplicates and requires idempotent sinks.

apiDetails.purpose: Append an ordered record to a partition leader.
apiDetails.rationale: acks=all waits for the in-sync replica set subject to min ISR; it is not an end-to-end exactly-once guarantee.

apiDetails.purpose: Fetch a bounded sequence of committed records.
apiDetails.rationale: Consumer groups own partition assignments; keep commit progress separate from fetch position.

steps.title: Producer apps → Broker cluster
steps.explanation: Send a keyed batch with producer sequence to the partition leader. Wait for configured ISR replication.

steps.title: Broker cluster → Consumer group
steps.explanation: Consumers fetch committed offsets and checkpoint only after their side effects are durable.

steps.title: Broker cluster → Controller (KRaft)
steps.explanation: The consensus controller chooses an eligible leader and publishes a new epoch. Producers refresh metadata and retry safely.

failureCases.scenario: A broker crashes after append but before the producer receives an ack
failureCases.handling: The producer retries with the same identity and sequence. Elect only an eligible replica; consumers may reprocess records after a rebalance, so sinks must dedup.

alternatives: Keep retained segments on broker disks for predictable local replay latency. Choose tiered storage for cheaper long retention, accepting object-store fetch latency and manifest coordination.
